title: The Sample That Spoiled the Graph
story: For a month the allotment trial gave steady nitrogen readings, until Thursday's sample from bed four came back far higher. Ivo wanted to drop it as contamination from a dirty tool. Sen told him not to discard a result merely because it spoiled a tidy graph. The bed stood by the compost gate, so a spill was possible, but possibility was not proof. The sampling notes said bed four had been taken last, with the same washed tool used on the earlier beds. They also recorded a manure pile against the fence that morning. The high reading could therefore be real. Ivo took a second sample and logged the pile. If the two results matched, the trial would treat bed four as genuinely richer, not as an error. Science, Sen said, begins by trying to disprove the convenient explanation.

vocabulary.definition: A nutrient in soil that this trial measured.
Unwanted material that spoils a result.
Collecting material so it can be tested.
Truly, and not only in appearance.
Show that an explanation is wrong.

quiz.question: What did the sampling notes say about the tool used on bed four?
options: The same washed tool had been used on the earlier beds
The tool had been left overnight in the compost
The tool belonged to a different laboratory
The tool was used for the first time on Friday
quiz.correctAnswer: The same washed tool had been used on the earlier beds
quiz.explanation: The notes said bed four was taken last with the same washed tool used on the earlier beds.
quiz.supportingSentence: The sampling notes said bed four had been taken last, with the same washed tool used on the earlier beds.

quiz.question: What must the trial do if the second result matches the first?
options: Treat bed four as truly richer soil
Close the allotment for the rest of the season
Blame the other beds for readings that are too low
Remove Thursday from the project entirely
quiz.correctAnswer: Treat bed four as truly richer soil
quiz.explanation: A match would mean the trial must treat bed four as genuinely richer, not as an error.
quiz.supportingSentence: If the two results matched, the trial would treat bed four as genuinely richer, not as an error.

quiz.question: Why does a possible spill fail to settle the high reading by itself?
options: A possible cause is not the same thing as proof
Sen had already published the Thursday figure
Manure is unable to change any soil test
Bed four had been removed before Thursday
quiz.correctAnswer: A possible cause is not the same thing as proof
quiz.explanation: A spill beside the compost gate was possible, but the story says possibility was not proof.
quiz.supportingSentence: The bed stood by the compost gate, so a spill was possible, but possibility was not proof.

quiz.question: What does discard mean when Sen talks about the odd result?
options: Throw it out and pay it no further attention
Copy it onto a second page of the log
Water the bed before taking the next test
Set it beside a chart of rainfall
quiz.correctAnswer: Throw it out and pay it no further attention
quiz.explanation: Sen tells Ivo not to discard the result, meaning not to throw it out, just because it spoils the graph.
quiz.supportingSentence: Sen told him not to discard a result merely because it spoiled a tidy graph.

quiz.question: Why does the writer mention the manure pile?
options: To show a real event that could explain the high reading
To prove Ivo spilled manure on the lab bench
To explain why an artist drew the graph
To show that bed four no longer held any soil
quiz.correctAnswer: To show a real event that could explain the high reading
quiz.explanation: The notes record manure against the fence that morning, which could make the high reading real.
quiz.supportingSentence: They also recorded a manure pile against the fence that morning.
